**DI110*** is a classification within the ICD-10 medical coding system used to identify cases of heart failure. In the context of Danish healthcare quality monitoring, it serves as a critical data point for tracking cardiovascular outcomes. Specifically, it is one of several diagnosis codes utilized to extract heart failure data from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret) [^src1].

Within the national quality improvement framework for atrial fibrillation, DI110* is a core component in defining heart failure hospital contacts. It is grouped alongside other related codes (such as DI50*, DI130*, DI132*, DI420*, DI426*, DI427*, DI428*, and DI429*) to identify instances where heart failure is recorded as either a primary (A) or secondary (B) diagnosis during a hospital visit [^src1]. 

This specific coding group is fundamentally linked to the [[hjertesvigtsindikatoren|Hjertesvigtsindikatoren]] (the heart failure indicator), which is designated as Indicator 15 in the 2025 AFDK report [^src1]. This indicator measures the incidence of heart failure within one year following a new diagnosis of atrial fibrillation, making the accurate capture of DI110* and its associated codes essential for evaluating the quality of cardiac care and identifying potential gaps in patient management across Denmark [^src1].
